title: Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope and Drainage Grade
description: Maintaining proper slope along horizontal drainage lines is essential for long-term system health. If a drain line is installed with insufficient pitch, water slows down, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle and form stubborn blockages. Conversely, an excessive slope allows liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solids behind. Routine maintenance includes inspecting pipe hangers for sagging or loose fasteners that cause belly points where standing water collects. Ensuring uniform support along the run preserves proper flow dynamics according to applicable building codes.

Maintaining Proper Pipe Slope and Drainage Grade

Maintaining proper slope along horizontal drainage lines is essential for long-term system health. If a drain line is installed with insufficient pitch, water slows down, allowing heavy solids and grease to settle and form stubborn blockages. Conversely, an excessive slope allows liquids to run off too quickly, leaving solids behind. Routine maintenance includes inspecting pipe hangers for sagging or loose fasteners that cause belly points where standing water collects. Ensuring uniform support along the run preserves proper flow dynamics according to applicable building codes.
